solver_rounds.brief: The solver ran the pooled screen, explained the co-visited plaza sites away as subsets of the pump's victims, re-screened the 78 victims the pump leaves and found the Lombard PIN pad, then checked the last 31 for a common point: 387 and every ask figure. The next rung would need a site that outranks the PIN pad on the residual and survives the subset check; any such site carries unexplained victims of its own and reads as a compromise (a fork), and any site that does not is dismissed by the subset check this solver already ran. The architecture is spent: re-root.

Missed at the decisive analytical step (rung 1): every field and stated rule read correctly (episodes, split postcodes, the extract day, the five-year expected count) and every ask figure right, but the solver set the cases notified so far against PR-07's expected count and sent the team to Wagga Wagga (7.6 against Griffith and Snowy Valleys 5.6) without a word on reporting delay. A valid analytical miss under the three rules. The proxy is high (65.2) because every ask is independent of the call: the slide's cluster list becomes the clusters in the area the team goes to (its school visits), so a wrong area carries a wrong list.

Missed at the decisive analytical step (rung 1) again, after the slide was made call-dependent: every field and stated rule read correctly (episodes, split postcodes, the extract day, the five-year expected count, the roster checks) and every CSV figure right, but the solver set the cases notified so far against PR-07's expected count and sent the team to Wagga Wagga (7.6 against Griffith and Snowy Valleys 5.6) without a word on reporting delay; the slide then carried Wagga Wagga's clusters (Wollundry 3, Bolton Park HS 2) instead of Griffith's (Banna Avenue 5, Kooyoo Street 2). Proxy fell from 65.2 to 59.0; the slide items still score partial token hits because the solver names Griffith as runner-up and shares 'Public School' tokens. A valid analytical miss under the three rules.
